merged.title: Match func_L00_001F5C60 (debug menu draw, 4,884 bytes)
merged.author: dev-gian
merged.untrustedBody:
`func_L00_001F5C60` matched byte-for-byte, in one commit. It is the largest function matched so far: 4,884 bytes, the debug menu draw in `src/overlays/shared/draw_001F3A78.c`.

Matched code goes from 78.629% to 78.760% (4,225 to 4,226 functions).

How it was found: the staged near miss in `nonmatching/shared/` was one byte off. decomp-permuter (via `tools/permuter_setup.py`) found a change that closes it, and I applied only that change to the readable source, with proper names:

- the format-string pointer `D_L00_0015F1D8` is cached in a local (`fmt`) on its first use in the ammo block, and later calls reuse it;
- the constant `16` in `D_0015EE84 * 16` is held in a local (`stride`).

The `volatile` global is the spin on a hardware status flag (`while (D_L00_00161260 & 1) {}`); without it the loop is removed and the size is wrong (4,900 against 4,884).

merged.title: fix(tools): link without objects on the command line; build programs in parallel
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Two changes to `tools/build.py`, and the docs that go with them.

## The linker stopped working past about 1,700 C functions

Every object was passed to `ld.exe` on the command line. With the functions now
on master that line is over 33,000 characters, and a Windows program accepts
32,767. Under Wine the SN linker then exits with an error and prints nothing, so
the build fails at the boot with an empty `link.log`.

The linker script already names every object it places, which is what loads
them, so the objects on the command line were redundant. They are gone. Output
is unchanged: all 28 programs still equal retail.

## Builds run in parallel

`tools/build.py all` and `levels` build several programs at once, each in its
own process (`--jobs N`, default half the cores, at most 8). Compiled objects
are moved into place whole, since two programs can compile the same shared file.

Measured on an 18-core Mac with the tools in containers: about 12 minutes
sequentially, about 7 at eight jobs.

Twenty level units matched at once, one worker each (bounded at 18 functions or 150 minutes per unit, as docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md describes). The units are the twenty level files with the most unmatched functions; every body was checked with `tools/check.py` at every place and then by the full build.

**What the batch measured, and it is now written into #157:**

- **The `sda` lever, confirmed independently by four workers.** Read the retail column first, then pick the profile: `lui $r,%hi` (absolute) means staying in the `-G0` file with `__attribute__((sda))` on the symbol - gas then folds `%hi/%lo` into the destination register and the emission order falls into place; `off($gp)` means the `-g8` sibling. It moves the register *and* the order, where rewording the C does not: four spellings of one body produced strictly identical bytes. Those helpers are inline assembly, and AGENTS.md's "Plain C" rule - no inline assembly in a function - rules that out as a matching route; `docs/COMPILER-NOTES.md` states it in as many words. They build, but they are not legitimate matches, so they go back to assembly here: `L07_003F4578.c` 4, `L03_00399230.c` 2, `L00_003EE100.c` 2, `L00_003FFA70.c` 2, and one each in `L05_00314E28.c`, `L06_00458138.c`, `L11_00453358.c`, `L16_00403900.c`, `L19_003E9400.c`, `L00_003B3158.c`, `L00_003E3258.c`.

Each body is kept in `nonmatching/` with a note saying why it cannot land, and the README gains a section for them: the shape is right, and only the 128-bit copies need a plain-C spelling that `mode(TI)` and the aggregate forms have not given yet. The markers are back in place, in their address order.

opened.title: feat(src): level functions from the seventh wave, twenty units in parallel
opened.author: llesieur99
opened.untrustedBody:
Twenty level units matched at once, one worker each (bounded at 18 functions or 150 minutes per unit, as docs/AGENT_WORKFLOW.md describes). The units are the twenty level files with the most unmatched functions; every body was checked with `tools/check.py` at every place and then by the full build.

**What the batch measured, and it is now written into #157:**

- **The `sda` lever, confirmed independently by four workers.** Read the retail column first, then pick the profile: `lui $r,%hi` (absolute) means staying in the `-G0` file with `__attribute__((sda))` on the symbol - gas then folds `%hi/%lo` into the destination register and the emission order falls into place; `off($gp)` means the `-g8` sibling. It moves the register *and* the order, where rewording the C does not: four spellings of one body produced strictly identical bytes. Its precondition was measured too: the attribute helps only when the symbol is read by that body alone - on a shared symbol it moved an already integrated

opened.title: docs(nonmatching): the wave notes in English, as the rules now ask
opened.author: llesieur99
opened.untrustedBody:
AGENTS.md gained the language rule in #161: everything that lands in the repository is in English, and it says the notes kept in `nonmatching/` are published material and follow the same rule. Thirty of the notes left by the six agent waves were still in the language their worker thought in - this translates them.

The prose is translated, the data is not: every register name, offset, byte count, instruction name and measured claim stays exactly as it stood, because those notes are the evidence behind each entry. Nothing else is touched - no C body, no detail added or dropped, and the files whose note was already in English are left alone.

Checked: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` (20 tests) and `tests/check_repository.py` pass, and a script compares every changed file's bytes below its leading comment against the committed revision, byte for byte: no difference. Not run: `tools/build.py all`, which `nonmatching/` does not take part in.

## Commits

- **Overlay sources and near misses laid out like rac1:** `src/overlays/shared/` holds code in two or more levels (48 files) and `src/overlays/lNN_<level>/` code in one level (29 files).
